fields.description_1:
Werkenbijalpinadrive is a recruitment site for driving professionals, so candidates need more than a list of open roles. They want to understand the employer, the type of driving work, practical conditions and what the application process looks like before sharing their details. Benefits can support that decision, but they should not replace role-specific information.

The website therefore needed to connect employer information with vacancy discovery without making candidates jump between unrelated pages. Mobile visitors also need vacancy cards and application actions to stay easy to follow. The portfolio story had to describe the candidate journey without inventing application growth, retention or employee satisfaction. The challenge was to help drivers judge whether the company and role fit them, then continue to an application with enough context.
fields.description_2:
I structured Werkenbijalpinadrive around the candidate's decision sequence. Employer information and the reality of the work provide context first, while vacancies lead into role details and a direct application path. Benefits and supporting content sit near the parts of the journey where they help someone evaluate the employer instead of becoming a generic promotional section.

The application action remains visible after candidates have enough information to decide whether a role is relevant. On mobile, vacancy cards, role details and form actions keep a simple order. The portfolio case now explains how WordPress supports recruitment for driving professionals through a focused employer-and-vacancy journey, without claiming more applications, faster hiring or better employee outcomes that were not independently measured.

fields.description_1:
Sodriveacademie trains prospective driving instructors, and those students need to understand more than the course name before enrolling. Requirements, programme content, planning and the route into the profession can all affect whether the training fits someone's situation. If those details are spread across pages, the decision becomes harder to follow.

The website therefore needed to connect orientation, course information and enrolment in a clear sequence. Practical requirements had to appear before a student reaches a form, while information needed to stay readable on mobile. The portfolio story also had to avoid claiming pass rates, job outcomes or guaranteed qualification results without evidence. The challenge was to turn a training offer into an understandable WordPress journey from first interest to an informed enrolment or contact decision.
fields.description_2:
I organised Sodriveacademie around the questions a prospective driving instructor is likely to ask before enrolling. The training route is introduced first, followed by course content, requirements, planning and practical details. Enrolment or contact actions appear after that information so the next step follows a real decision instead of a promotional push.

Supporting content stays close to the stage it explains, and the mobile layout keeps programme sections and actions easy to scan. I used plain labels rather than educational jargon where a simpler phrase works. The portfolio case now shows how WordPress supports a structured training journey for future instructors, while avoiding unsupported claims about exam success, employment, learning speed or qualification outcomes that depend on the student and external assessment.

fields.description_1:
Furkaneducatie supports students and parents through courses, tutoring and learning programmes. Families may arrive with questions about age, subject or format, so a single overview of everything offered would not help them decide which route fits. The language also needs to stay clear for families.

The website therefore needed to separate programmes while keeping registration and contact easy to reach after useful context. Practical details had to support the choice instead of appearing only at the end of the site. On mobile, programme cards and forms needed a predictable order. The portfolio story had to avoid claiming grade improvement, exam success or learning outcomes without evidence. The challenge was to make several education routes understandable to students and parents without sounding like generic school marketing.
fields.description_2:
I structured Furkaneducatie around distinct learning programmes so students and parents can start with the type of support they are considering. Course and tutoring information explains the purpose, practical details and next step before a registration or contact action appears. Shared information stays available without repeating the same introduction on every programme page.

This keeps the site useful for families comparing options rather than forcing them through a long institutional story. On smaller screens, programme cards, details and forms follow the same hierarchy. I kept the language direct and avoided promises about marks, exam results or educational progress that require individual evidence. The portfolio case now describes how WordPress organises multiple learning routes and registration decisions in a clear, family-friendly structure.

fields.description_1:
Tasveren is a WooCommerce shop where customers browse bags and accessories that are often chosen visually. Strong imagery is important, but it can make comparison difficult if size, price, variation or practical product details are not easy to find. A shopper should not need to open pages just to understand the difference between similar items.

The webshop therefore needed a path from category discovery to product detail and cart actions, with visual choice and factual information working together. Mobile screens make that balance more important because large images can push controls out of view. The portfolio story had to avoid claiming sales or conversion improvements without data. The challenge was to keep a visual retail experience attractive while making product selection and purchase decisions straightforward.
fields.description_2:
I organised Tasveren around simple product discovery and comparison. Categories provide the first filter, while product pages combine imagery with the price, variations and practical details needed before adding an item to the cart. Visual choices remain prominent, but they do not replace the information a shopper needs to understand what is being purchased.

On mobile, product cards, variation controls and cart actions keep a consistent order so the buying task stays visible beneath the imagery. Secondary content sits outside the main shopping path unless it helps a product decision. The portfolio case now explains how WooCommerce supports a visually led bag and accessory shop without relying on generic ecommerce language or unsupported claims about conversion, customer preference, repeat purchases or sales growth.

fields.description_1:
Leercentrum offers programmes and guidance to students and parents who may not know which support fits their situation. Programme names, age groups and practical arrangements can quickly create too many choices if they are shown without a hierarchy. Parents also need enough context before completing a registration or contact form.

The website therefore needed to separate learning routes and make guidance information easy to understand in plain language. Practical details had to remain close to the programme they describe, especially on mobile where long education pages are difficult to scan. The portfolio story also had to avoid promises about grades, exams or learning speed. The challenge was to turn several educational options into a clear decision path for families without making unsupported outcome claims.
fields.description_2:
I structured Leercentrum around the learning route first, then the guidance and practical information that support the choice. Each programme can explain who it is for, what kind of support it provides and what a parent or learner should do next. Registration or contact actions follow that context rather than appearing before the programme is understood.

Shared guidance remains accessible without duplicating the same text across every route. On smaller screens, programme cards, details and forms keep a readable sequence. I used direct headings and avoided claims about guaranteed improvement or exam success. The portfolio case now shows how WordPress can organise several learning options for students and parents in a way that is easy to compare, understand and act on without generic education marketing.
